modules.title: Module 1: Pinyin and Tones
modules.content:
## Why Pinyin Matters  

Imagine you are standing in a bustling Shanghai night market. A vendor calls out “**xiǎo lǐ**!” You think you heard “xiaoli,” but the tone is wrong, and the vendor smiles politely while you order a wrong dish. In Mandarin, **tone** is as important as the consonant or vowel itself—one mis‑tone can change *“mother”* (mā) into *“horse”* (mǎ). Mastering **pinyin**, the Roman alphabet system that maps Chinese sounds, gives you a reliable “pronunciation compass” so you can navigate any conversation without getting lost.

---

## The Building Blocks: Initials and Finals  

Pinyin separates a syllable into two parts:

* **Initial** – the consonant that begins the syllable.  
* **Final** – the vowel (or vowel‑plus‑final‑consonant) that follows the initial.  

Together they form a **syllable**, the basic spoken unit in Mandarin. There are **21 initials** and **35 finals** that combine to produce all possible Mandarin syllables (excluding tone).

### 21 Initials  

| Initial | Example | Note |
|---------|---------|------|
| b | **b**ā (八) | Unaspirated, like English *b* |
| p | **p**ā (爬) | Aspirated, a burst of air |
| m | **m**ā (妈) | Same as English *m* |
| f | **f**ā (发) | Same as English *f* |
| d | **d**ā (大) | Unaspirated *d* |
| t | **t**ā (他) | Aspirated *t* |
| n | **n**ā (哪) | Same as English *n* |
| l | **l**ā (啦) | Same as English *l* |
| g | **g**ā (嘎) | Unaspirated *g* |
| k | **k**ā (卡) | Aspirated *k* |
| h | **h**ā (哈) | Like a soft *h* |
| j | **j**i (鸡) | Palatal, no English equivalent |
| q | **q**i (七) | Aspirated palatal |
| x | **x**i (西) | Palatal, like a soft *sh* |
| zh | **zh**ī (知) | Retroflex *j* sound |
| ch | **ch**ī (吃) | Aspirated retroflex |
| sh | **sh**ī (时) | Retroflex *sh* |
| r | **r**i (日) | Similar to *zh* but with a “r” quality |
| z | **z**i (子) | Unaspirated alveolar affricate |
| c | **c**i (次) | Aspirated alveolar affricate |
| s | **s**i (思) | Same as English *s* |

> **Tip:** The letters *j, q, x* never appear with a final that begins with *i* or *u*; they always pair with the “i‑like” finals listed below.

### 35 Finals  

| Final | Example | Note |
|-------|---------|------|
| a | **a** (啊) | Open central vowel |
| o | **o** (喔) | Rounded back vowel |
| e | **e** (鹅) | Mid front vowel |
| i | **i** (衣) | High front vowel |
| u | **u** (乌) | High back vowel |
| ü | **ü** (迂) | Front rounded vowel (write as **v** on keyboards) |
| ai | **ai** (爱) | Diphthong |
| ei | **ei** (诶) | Diphthong |
| ao | **ao** (奥) | Diphthong |
| ou | **ou** (欧) | Diphthong |
| an | **an** (安) | Nasal vowel |
| en | **en** (恩) | Nasal vowel |
| ang | **ang** (昂) | Nasal vowel |
| eng | **eng** (恩) | Nasal vowel |
| er | **er** (儿) | Retroflex vowel |
| ia | **ia** (呀) | Combines *i* + *a* |
| ie | **ie** (叶) | *i* + *e* |
| iao | **iao** (iao) | *i* + *ao* |
| iou (iu) | **iu** (有) | *i* + *ou* |
| ian | **ian** (言) | *i* + *an* |
| in | **in** (因) | *i* + *n* |
| iang | **iang** (央) | *i* + *ang* |
| ing | **ing** (英) | *i* + *ng* |
| uang | **uang** (王) | *u* + *ang* |
| uei (ui) | **ui** (为) | *u* + *ei* |
| uan | **uan** (玩) | *u* + *an* |
| un | **un** (云) | *u* + *n* |
| ueng | **ueng** (翁) | *u* + *eng* |
| üe | **üe** (约) | *ü* + *e* |
| ün | **ün** (晕) | *ü* + *n* |
| er (retroflex) | **er** (而) | Same as final *er* above |
| i (as a final) | **i** (一) | Used after certain initials |
| u (as a final) | **u** (乌) | Used after certain initials |
| ü (as a final) | **ü** (迂) | Same as above |

> **Note:** In practice, the finals *iu, ui, and üe* are often written with the shortened forms *iu → **iu**, ui → **ui**, üe → **üe**. When typing on a standard QWERTY keyboard, **ü** is entered as **v** (e.g., “lv” for “lü”).

### Writing Practice  

1. **Copy** each initial–final pair on a lined notebook.  
2. **Pronounce** the pair aloud, matching the tone mark you will learn later.  
3. **Check** your spelling against the table; a single misplaced letter changes the meaning entirely.

---

## Mastering the Four Tones (and the Neutral Tone)  

Mandarin has **four lexical tones** plus a **neutral (light) tone**. The tone is indicated in pinyin by a diacritic placed over the vowel of the final.

| Tone | Symbol | Pitch Contour (visual) | Example (ma) | Meaning |
|------|--------|------------------------|--------------|---------|
| First | **¯** (macron) | High, level → ——— | **mā** (妈) | “mother” |
| Second | **´** (acute) | Rising → ↗ | **má** (麻) | “hemp” |
| Third | **ˇ** (caron) | Low‑then‑rising → ↘↗ | **mǎ** (马) | “horse” |
| Fourth | **`** (grave) | Falling → ↘ | **mà** (骂) | “scold” |
| Neutral | (none) | Light, quick | **ma** (吗) – question particle | “? ” |

### Listening Exercise  

1. **Audio File 1** – “ma” in the five tones.  
2. **Audio File 2** – Minimal pairs: *bā* vs *bá* vs *bǎ* vs *bà*.  
3. **Audio File 3** – Neutral‑tone words in natural speech (e.g., “shénme” – 什么).  

> **Action:** Play each file, pause after hearing a tone, and repeat the syllable aloud. Record yourself and compare the waveform (most language‑learning apps show pitch).

### Common Pitfalls  

* **Tone‑merging** – When two tones appear consecutively, the second may be reduced.  
* **Over‑emphasis** – Beginners often hold the first tone too long; keep it short and steady.  
* **Neutral‑tone confusion** – It carries no diacritic; rely on context and rhythm.

---

## Putting It Together: 50 Common Syllables with Correct Tone Marks  

Below is a curated list of 50 frequently encountered syllables. Each entry shows the pinyin with tone mark, the corresponding character (for reference), and an English gloss. Practice each aloud, paying attention to the tone diacritic.

| # | Pinyin | Character | Gloss |
|---|--------|-----------|-------|
| 1 | **bā** | 爸 | dad |
| 2 | **bá** | 把 | to hold |
| 3 | **bǎ** | 把 | (particle) |
| 4 | **bà** | 爸 | (dialect) |
| 5 | **mā** | 妈 | mother |
| 6 | **má** | 麻 | hemp |
| 7 | **mǎ** | 马 | horse |
| 8 | **mà** | 骂 | scold |
| 9 | **hā** | 哈 | laugh |
|10 | **hóu** | 侯 | marquis |
|11 | **hǒu** | 候 | wait |
|12 | **hòu** | 后 | behind |
|13 | **shì** | 是 | to be |
|14 | **shí** | 十 | ten |
|15 | **shǐ** | 使 | to make |
|16 | **shì** (neutral) | 吗 | question particle |
|17 | **lǐ** | 里 | inside |
|18 | **lì** | 力 | strength |
|19 | **lǐ** (neutral) | 里 (as particle) |
|20 | **tī** | 提 | to lift |
|21 | **tí** | 提 | to mention |
|22 | **tǐ** | 体 | body |
|23 | **tì** | 替 | to replace |
|24 | **gē** | 歌 | song |
|25 | **gé** | 格 | pattern |
|26 | **gě** | 给 | give |
|27 | **gè** | 个 | classifier |
|28 | **kā** | 咖 | (part of “kāfēi”) |
|29 | **kǎ** | 卡 | card |
|30 | **kà** | 咖 (tone‑sandhi) |
|31 | **zǎo** | 早 | early |
|32 | **zāo** | 糟 | messy |
|33 | **zào** | 造 | to create |
|34 | **cǎi** | 彩 | color |
|35 | **cái** | 才 | talent |
|36 | **cài** | 菜 | vegetable |
|37 | **rén** | 人 | person |
|38 | **rè** | 热 | hot |
|39 | **rǔ** | 如 (neutral) |
|40 | **yú** | 鱼 | fish |
|41 | **yǔ** | 雨 | rain |
|42 | **yù** | 预 | to anticipate |
|43 | **wǒ** | 我 | I/me |
|44 | **wò** | 握 | to grip |
|45 | **wò** (neutral) | 我 (tone sandhi) |
|46 | **qī** | 七 | seven |
|47 | **qí** | 旗 | flag |

|50 | **dē** | 的 (neutral) | possessive particle |

> **Practice Routine:**  
> 1. **Listen** to the audio file that reads the list in order.  
> 2. **Shadow** – repeat each syllable immediately after hearing it.  
> 3. **Write** the pinyin with tone marks three times from memory.  
> 4. **Check** against the table; correct any mismarked tones.

---

## Tone Sandhi in Action: Simple Two‑Syllable Words  

**Tone sandhi** (tone change) occurs when tones interact in connected speech. The most frequent pattern for beginners is the **“Third‑Tone Sandhi.”**  

### Rule: Third‑Tone Sandhi  

- When two third tones appear consecutively, the first one is pronounced as a **second tone** (rising).  
- Example: **nǐ hǎo** (你好) is actually pronounced **ní hǎo**.

#### Step‑by‑Step Illustration  

| Original Pinyin | Literal Tones | Sandhi Applied | Pronounced As |
|-----------------|----------------|----------------|---------------|
| **nǐ hǎo** | 3rd + 3rd | First 3rd → 2nd | **ní hǎo** |
| **lǎo shī** (老师) | 3rd + 1st | No change (only first is 3rd) | **lǎo shī** |
| **hěn hǎo** (很好) | 3rd + 3rd | First 3rd → 2nd | **hén hǎo** |

### Other Common Sandhi Patterns  

| Pattern | Description | Example |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| **“不” (bù) → 2nd tone before 4th tone** | The negative particle **bù** normally has a fourth tone, but changes to second tone when followed by a fourth tone. | **bù qù** → **bú qù** (“don’t go”) |
| **“一” (yī) tone changes** | **yī** is 1st tone alone, becomes 2nd tone before a 4th tone, and 4th tone before any other tone. | **yī ge** → **yì ge**; **yī shì** → **yí shì** |
| **“了” (le) neutral** | Always neutral, regardless of surrounding tones. | **hǎo le** (“good now”) |

### Quick Drill  

1. **Read** the pair “bù qù”.  
2. **Identify** the tone of the second syllable (4th).  
3. **Apply** the rule → pronounce **bú qù**.  

Repeat this drill with the following list:

1. **bù shì** → **bú shì**  
2. **yī zhōng** → **yì zhōng**  
3. **yī fēn** → **yí fēn**  

### Why Sandhi Matters  

Even if you know each syllable’s tone, ignoring sandhi will make you sound “robotic” and can cause misunderstandings. In everyday speech, native speakers apply these changes automatically; training your ear and mouth now builds that automaticity.

---

## Practice Tips & Resources  

| Strategy | How to Implement |
|----------|------------------|
| **Chunked Listening** | Break audio into 2‑syllable segments; repeat until the sandhi feels natural. |
| **Tone‑Color Visualization** | Imagine each tone as a color (1st = red, 2nd = orange, 3rd = blue, 4th = purple). Visual cue helps memory. |
| **Mobile Apps** | Use apps that show pitch curves (e.g., Pleco, HelloChinese). Compare your recording to the native curve. |
| **Peer Feedback** | Pair up with a classmate; take turns recording a list of syllables and rating each other’s tone accuracy. |
| **Flashcards with Audio** | Create digital flashcards where the front shows the pinyin **without** tone marks, the back reveals the marked version and plays the audio. |

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Pinyin** splits a Mandarin syllable into **21 initials** and **35 finals**; mastering their spelling is the foundation for accurate pronunciation.  
- Mandarin has **four lexical tones** plus a **neutral tone**; each tone follows a distinct pitch contour that changes meaning.  
- **Audio exposure** is essential—listen, repeat, and record to internalize the tones.  
- The **50 common syllables** listed provide a practical repertoire; practice them with tone marks until they become second nature.  
- **Tone sandhi** (especially the third‑tone sandhi) modifies tones in connected speech; apply the rule “3‑tone → 2‑tone” and remember the special cases for **bù** and **yī**.  
- Consistent, focused practice—using listening drills, visual aids, and peer feedback—will turn the abstract tone system into fluent, natural speech.

modules.title: Module 2: Basic Greetings and Self‑Introduction
modules.content:
## 1. A Morning Meet‑up: Why a Good Greeting Matters  

Imagine you arrive at a community centre for a Chinese‑language exchange. The host, **Lǐ xiǎo lǐ**, smiles and says, “**早上好！**” You feel instantly welcomed, and the conversation flows. The opposite—stumbling over a greeting or using the wrong time‑of‑day phrase—can make the exchange feel awkward. This chapter equips you with the three core time‑specific greetings, plus the set‑ups you’ll need to introduce yourself politely and close a conversation gracefully.

---

## 2. Time‑of‑Day Greetings  

| English | Mandarin (Characters) | Pinyin | Tone marks* |
|---------|------------------------|--------|-------------|
| Good morning | 早上好 | zǎo shàng hǎo | 3‑4‑3 |
| Good afternoon | 下午好 | xià wǔ hǎo | 4‑3‑3 |
| Good evening / Good night (when meeting) | 晚上好 | wǎn shàng hǎo | 3‑4‑3 |

*Tone marks follow the four‑tone system introduced in Module 1.  

### 2.1 Pronunciation Checklist  

1. **早 (zǎo)** – the “ao” final carries the third tone; start low, dip, then rise.  
2. **下午 (xià wǔ)** – “xià” is fourth tone (sharp fall), “wǔ” is third tone.  
3. **晚上 (wǎn shàng)** – “wǎn” third tone, “shàng” fourth tone.  

> **Tip:** Practice each phrase in isolation, then pair it with a friendly smile. Tone‑sandhi (tone changes) does not apply here; keep the tones as listed.

### 2.2 When to Use Each Greeting  

| Time Range | Preferred Greeting |
|------------|-------------------|
| 5 a.m. – 11 a.m. | 早上好 |
| 12 p.m. – 5 p.m. | 下午好 |
| After 5 p.m. (until bedtime) | 晚上好 |

If you’re unsure, “你好” (nǐ hǎo) works any time, but the specific greetings show cultural awareness.

---

## 3. Introducing Yourself  

Two structures dominate beginner self‑introduction:

1. **我叫 …** – “My name is …” (used for full names or nicknames).  
2. **我是 …** – “I am …” (used for nationality, occupation, or role).

### 3.1 Vocabulary Cheat‑Sheet  

| English | Mandarin | Pinyin | Note |
|---------|----------|--------|------|
| I (subject) | 我 | wǒ | 3rd tone |
| called / name is | 叫 | jiào | 4th tone |
| am (identity) | 是 | shì | 4th tone |
| Chinese (nationality) | 中国人 | Zhōng guó rén | 1‑1‑2 |
| American (nationality) | 美国人 | Měi guó rén | 3‑2‑2 |
| teacher | 老师 | lǎo shī | 3‑1 |
| student | 学生 | xué shēng | 2‑1 |
| engineer | 工程师 | gōng chéng shī | 1‑2‑1 |

### 3.2 Step‑by‑Step: “I’m … from …”  

1. **State your name** – *我叫* + **your name**.  
   - Example: **我叫李明。** (Wǒ jiào Lǐ Míng.)  
2. **Declare nationality** – *我是* + **nationality** + **人**.  
   - Example: **我是美国人。** (Wǒ shì Měi guó rén.)  
3. **Add occupation (optional)** – *我是* + **occupation**.  
   - Example: **我是老师。** (Wǒ shì lǎo shī.)  

**Combined example:**  
> **我叫李明，我是美国人，我是老师。**  
> (Wǒ jiào Lǐ Míng, wǒ shì Měi guó rén, wǒ shì lǎo shī.)  
> “My name is Li Ming, I am American, I am a teacher.”

### 3.3 Practice Dialogue  

| Speaker | Mandarin | Pinyin |
|--------|----------|--------|
| A (host) | 早上好！ | Zǎo shàng hǎo! |
| A | 我叫李小莉，你好！ | Wǒ jiào Lǐ xiǎo lì, nǐ hǎo! |
| B (you) | 早上好！我叫**Anna**，我是**英国人**，我是一名**学生**。 | Zǎo shàng hǎo! Wǒ jiào Anna, wǒ shì Yīng guó rén, wǒ shì xué shēng. |
| A | 很高兴认识你！ | Hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ! |

Notice the repeated use of “我叫” and “我是” – the pattern stays the same even as the content changes.

---

## 4. Asking “How are you?” Politely  

### 4.1 Core Question  

- **你好吗？** (nǐ hǎo ma?) – literally “Are you good?”  
- Alternative, slightly more formal: **您好吗？** (nín hǎo ma?) – “您” is the polite “you”.

Both use the **吗** particle to turn a statement into a yes‑no question (see Module 1 for the particle’s function).

### 4.2 Expected Answers  

| Response | Mandarin | Pinyin | When to use |
|----------|----------|--------|-------------|
| I’m fine, thank you. | 我很好，谢谢。 | wǒ hěn hǎo, xièxiè. | Standard reply |
| I’m okay. | 我还好。 | wǒ hái hǎo. | When you’re not feeling great but don’t want to elaborate |
| Not so well. | 我不太好。 | wǒ bù tài hǎo. | If you feel unwell or want to be honest |

**Tip:** Adding “谢谢” after the answer shows gratitude for the concern, a habit that Chinese speakers appreciate.

### 4.3 Mini‑Conversation  

| Person A | 你好！你好吗？ |
|----------|--------------|
| Person B | 我很好，谢谢。你呢？ |
| Person A | 我也很好。 |

Notice the mirrored structure—once you master the pattern, you can plug in any adjective (好, 累, 忙, etc.) to describe your state.

---

## 5. Polite Closings  

### 5.1 Essential Farewells  

| English | Mandarin | Pinyin |
|---------|----------|--------|
| Goodbye / See you later | 再见 | zài jiàn |
| Thank you (formal) | 谢谢 | xiè xiè |
| You’re welcome | 不客气 | bù kè qì |
| Take care (informal) | 保重 | bǎo zhòng |

### 5.2 Using “再见” in Context  

1. **Finish a conversation** – After a brief exchange, say “**再见**”。  
2. **Signal a pause** – If you must step away temporarily, add “**我先走了，再见**” (wǒ xiān zǒu le, zài jiàn).  

### 5.3 Full Closing Example  

> **A:** 好的，今天聊得很开心。**谢谢**你的帮助。  
> **B:** 不客气！**再见**，祝你有美好的一天。  

Both parties end on a polite note, reinforcing a positive impression.

---

## 6. Practice Corner  

### 6.1 Fill‑in‑the‑Blanks  

Complete each sentence with the appropriate word(s).  

1. _______好！ (Good morning)  
2. 我叫______，我是______人。 (My name is …, I am …)  
3. 你______吗？ (How are you?)  
4. 我______，谢谢。 (I’m fine, thank you)  
5. 再______！ (Goodbye)

**Answers:** 1. 早上, 2. (your name) / (your nationality), 3. 好, 4. 很好, 5. 见  

### 6.2 Role‑Play Prompt  

You are meeting a new classmate at a university orientation. Use the following sequence:

1. Greet according to the time of day.  
2. Introduce your name, nationality, and major (use “我叫…”, “我是…”).  
3. Ask “How are you?” and reply with a brief answer.  
4. Close the conversation with “谢谢” and “再见”.  

Write out the full dialogue in Mandarin, then read it aloud, paying attention to the tones you learned in Module 1.

---

## 7. Cultural Notes  

- **时间感** (shíjiān gǎn) – Chinese people often emphasize punctuality. Arriving a few minutes early and greeting with the correct time‑of‑day phrase signals respect.  
- **Politeness hierarchy** – Using **您** instead of **你** when speaking to elders or strangers is a quick way to show deference.  
- **“谢谢” vs. “多谢”** – “谢谢” is the everyday “thank you”. “多谢” feels slightly more earnest, often used when someone has done you a favor.

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Three core greetings:** 早上好, 下午好, 晚上好 – match them to the clock.  
- **Self‑introduction patterns:**  
  - *我叫 [Name]* for names.  
  - *我是 [Nationality] 人* for nationality.  
  - *我是 [Occupation]* for jobs or roles.  
- **Polite inquiry:** *你好吗？* / *您好吗？* and respond with *我很好，谢谢* (or variations).  
- **Closing phrases:** *谢谢* (thank you) and *再见* (goodbye) are indispensable for a courteous exit.  
- Practice each phrase in isolation, then weave them into short dialogues. Mastery of tone, timing, and the “我叫 / 我是” structures will give you confidence to start any Mandarin conversation.

modules.title: Module 3: Numbers, Dates, and Time
modules.content:
## 开场情景：约朋友喝咖啡

小李和刚认识的同学 **Mia** 想在北京的咖啡店见面。  
他们需要确定：

1. **哪天** 合适？  
2. **几点** 开始？  
3. 约会要 **多久**？

这看似简单的日常安排，却涉及 **数字、日期、时间** 以及 **量词**——本章的全部学习目标。下面我们一步步拆解，让你在真实对话中自信表达。

---

## 1. 从 1 到 100 的基数数字

### 1.1 基本数字表（1‑10）

| 汉字 | 拼音 | 听写练习 |
|------|------|----------|
| 一   | yī   | ___ |
| 二   | èr   | ___ |
| 三   | sān  | ___ |
| 四   | sì   | ___ |
| 五   | wǔ   | ___ |
| 六   | liù  | ___ |
| 七   | qī   | ___ |
| 八   | bā   | ___ |
| 九   | jiǔ  | ___ |
| 十   | shí  | ___ |

> **Tip**：1‑10 的发音已经在 **Module 1** 的声调练习中出现，记得再次对照声调表确认声调准确。

### 1.2 十一到十九的构造

> 结构：**十 + 一位数**（如 **十一** = shí‑yī）

| 汉字 | 拼音 | 解释 |
|------|------|------|
| 十一 | shí‑yī | 11 |
| 十二 | shí‑èr | 12 |
| …    | …      | …   |
| 十九 | shí‑jiǔ | 19 |

**练习**：把下面的阿拉伯数字写成汉字并朗读  
`14, 17, 18`

### 1.3 整十：二十、三十…九十

> 结构：**十位数 + 十**（如 **二十** = èr‑shí）

| 汉字 | 拼音 |
|------|------|
| 二十 | èr‑shí |
| 三十 | sān‑shí |
| 四十 | sì‑shí |
| 五十 | wǔ‑shí |
| 六十 | liù‑shí |
| 七十 | qī‑shí |
| 八十 | bā‑shí |
| 九十 | jiǔ‑shí |

### 1.4 组合：21‑99

> 规则：**十位 + 十 + 个位**（若个位是“一”，可省略“一”）  
> 例：**二十一** = èr‑shí‑yī，**三十五** = sān‑shí‑wǔ，**七十** = qī‑shí（不加“一”）

**练习**：说出下面数字的中文读法  
`23, 40, 58, 71, 99`

### 1.5 百

| 汉字 | 拼音 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 一百 | yī‑bǎi | 100 |
| 一百零一 | yī‑bǎi‑líng‑yī | 101（本章不必记，后续会涉及） |

> **Note**：本章只要求掌握 **1‑100**，因此只需记 **一百**。

---

## 2. 中文日期的阅读与书写

### 2.1 日期的基本结构

中文的日期顺序是 **年‑月‑日**（Year‑Month‑Day），与西方的 **Month‑Day‑Year** 完全相反。  
常用的标记词：

| 标记词 | 含义 |
|--------|------|
| 年 (nián) | 年 |
| 月 (yuè) | 月 |
| 日 (rì) / 号 (hào) | 日 |

> **Tip**：**日** 与 **号** 在口语中常互换，**号** 更口语化。

### 2.2 书写示例

| 阿拉伯数字 | 中文写法 | 朗读 |
|------------|----------|------|
| 2024‑04‑12 | 二零二四年四月十二日 | èr‑líng‑èr‑sì nián sì‑yuè shí‑èr rì |
| 1999‑12‑31 | 一九九九年十二月三十一日 | yī‑jiǔ‑jiǔ‑jiǔ nián shí‑èr yuè sān‑shí‑yī rì |

**练习**：把以下日期写成中文并朗读  
`2023‑07‑01, 2025‑11‑20`

### 2.3 口头表达的简化

在日常对话中，人们往往省略 **年**，直接说 **几月几号**：

- **四月十二号** (sì‑yuè shí‑èr hào)  
- **十一月三十** (shí‑yī‑yuè sān‑shí rì)

**对话示例**  

> **小李**：我们什么时候见面？  
> **Mia**：这个 **四月十二号** 下午三点怎么样？

---

## 3. 询问与表达时间

### 3.1 “几点？”——问时间

| 句型 | 解释 |
|------|------|
| 现在几点？ | “What time is it now?” |
| 你几点到？ | “What time will you arrive?” |

**回答模板**  

- **整点**：**[小时] 点**（如 **三点**）  
- **半点**：**[小时] 点半**（如 **三点半**）  
- **分钟**：**[小时] 点 [分钟] 分**（如 **三点十五分**）

> **Tip**：**点** (diǎn) 表示小时，**分** (fēn) 表示分钟。记得 **半** (bàn) 只用于 **半点**。

### 3.2 常见时间表达

| 中文 | 拼音 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 1:00 | yī diǎn | 1 o’clock |
| 2:30 | liǎng diǎn bàn | 2 : 30 |
| 4:15 | sì diǎn yī shí wǔ fēn | 4 : 15 |
| 7:45 | qī diǎn sì shí wǔ fēn | 7 : 45 |

**练习**：把下列时间用中文说出来  
`5:00, 9:30, 12:05, 6:45`

### 3.3 表达**时长**（持续多久）

| 单位 | 汉字 | 拼音 |
|------|------|------|
| 小时 | 小时 | xiǎo‑shí |
| 分钟 | 分钟 | fēn‑zhōng |
| 天 | 天 | tiān |
| 周 | 周 | zhōu |
| 个月 | 个月 | gè‑yuè |

#### 3.3.1 基本结构

**[数量] + [时间单位]**  

- **两个小时** (liǎng gè xiǎo shí) – 2 hours  
- **半个小时** (bàn gè xiǎo shí) – half an hour  
- **三天** (sān tiān) – 3 days  

> **Note**：在 **小时** 前常用 **个** 作为量词；在 **天、周、个月** 前则直接使用数字。

#### 3.3.2 例句

- 我**要等两个小时**。 (Wǒ yào děng liǎng gè xiǎo shí.) – “I’ll wait for two hours.”
- 这本书**读了三天**。 (Zhè běn shū dú le sān tiān.) – “I read the book for three days.”

### 3.4 综合对话：安排见面

> **小李**：我们 **四月十二号** 下午 **三点半** 在咖啡店见，怎么样？  
> **Mia**：好啊，我 **大约需要半个小时** 才能到。  
> **小李**：好的，等你。

---

## 4. 初步量词介绍（人数、物品、时间）

量词是汉语里 **名词前的“计量单位”**，类似英文的 “a / an”。本章只涉及以下几类：

| 类别 | 常用量词 | 示例 |
|------|----------|------|
| 人 | **位** (wèi) – 敬称；**个** (gè) – 非正式 | **三位老师** (sān wèi lǎo shī) |
| 一般物体 | **个** (gè) – 最常用；**本** (běn) – 书籍；**张** (zhāng) – 纸张、票 | **两本书** (liǎng běn shū) |
| 时间 | **个** (gè) – 小时；**分钟** (fēn zhōng) – 分钟；**天** (tiān) – 天数 | **三个小时** (sān gè xiǎo shí) |

> **Tip**：虽然完整的量词系统将在 **Module 4** 学习，你现在只需要记住 **位、个、分钟、天** 这几种，以便在本章的对话中使用。

---

## 5. 实战练习：从数字到约会

### 5.1 填空练习

把括号内的数字写成中文并补全句子。

1. 我们约在 **(2024‑04‑12)** ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___

2. 我们 **(14:30)** ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___

3. 这次旅行我们要 **(5 天)** ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___

*(答案请自行核对。)*

### 5.2 小对话写作

用本章学到的词汇和结构，写一段 **两人** 约定 **周末** 去 **图书馆** 学习的对话（不少于 8 句），并标注出所有数字、日期、时间以及使用的量词。

---

## 6. 发音小贴士：数字与声调的常见误区

1. **二** (èr) 与 **五** (wǔ) 的声调相同（四声），但 **二** 的尾音略带**儿化**（在北方口音中常听到 **'èr'**），记得不要把它读成 **'yī'**。  
2. **十** (shí) 的声调是 **二声**，在 **十一、十二** 中保持二声；但 **十五** 中的 **五** 仍是 **三声**，声调不受前面的 **十** 影响。  
3. **半** (bàn) 的四声在 **半点** 中常被快速说成 **bàn diǎn**，不要把 **半** 读成 **bān**（第一声）。  
4. **点** (diǎn) 的三声在 **几点** 中常被连读，保持三声清晰可帮助听者辨认。

---

## 7. 综合练习：真实情境模拟

> **情境**：你是 **小李**，需要给 **Mia** 发一条短信，内容包括：  
> - 确认 **4 月 12 日** 见面  
> - 约定 **下午 3 点半** 开始  
> - 说明你会等 **半个小时**  

**请写出完整的中文短信**（不少于 30 字），并在括号内标注每个数字的拼音。

*示例答案（仅供参考）*  
> Mia，咱们 **四月十二号** 下午 **三点半** 在咖啡店见面吧，我会等 **半个小时**（bàn gè xiǎo shí）。  

---

## Key Takeaways

- **数字** 1‑100 的读法遵循十位+个位的规律；**十一至十九** 直接在 **十** 后加个位，**二十、三十** 等整十则省略个位的 **一**。  
- **中文日期** 按 **年‑月‑日** 排列，常用标记词 **年、月、日/号**，口语中可省略 **年**。  
- **询问时间** 使用 **几点**；**回答** 结构为 **[小时] 点**、**[小时] 点半** 或 **[小时] 点 [分钟] 分**。  
- **时长** 表达为 **数量 + 时间单位**（小时、分钟、天等），常见量词包括 **个**（小时）和 **分钟、天**（直接使用）。  
- 初步 **量词**（位、个、分钟、天）足以支撑本章的对话，让你在安排约会、描述持续时间时更加自然。  

掌握这些要点后，你就能在日常生活中自如地 **数数、写日期、说时间**，为更复杂的中文交流奠定坚实基础。祝你练习愉快！

modules.title: Module 4: Everyday Nouns and Measure Words
modules.content:
## A Real‑World Moment: Ordering Lunch at a Busy Café You’ve just arrived at a bustling café in Shanghai. The menu is a colorful grid of dishes, drinks, and snacks. The server smiles and asks, “请问您要点什么？” (qǐng wèn nín yào diǎn shénme? – *What would you like to order?*). To answer confidently you need three things: 1. **The right noun** – “two bowls of noodles” → *两碗面条*. 2. **The correct measure word** – *碗* (wǎn) for bowls. 3. **The proper number** – *两* (liǎng) from the numbers you learned in Module 3. If you mix up the measure word, the sentence sounds odd: *两本面条* (two **books** of noodles) is clearly wrong. This short exchange illustrates why everyday nouns and their measure words are essential for natural Chinese conversation. Below you will meet **80 high‑frequency nouns** that appear in daily life, learn the **core measure words** for people, flat objects, and long objects, and practice building simple noun phrases such as “三本书” and “两杯水”. --- ## 1. Core Vocabulary: 80 Everyday Nouns The nouns are grouped by theme. Each entry shows the Chinese characters, **pinyin** (with tone marks you already mastered in Module 1), and the English meaning. ### 1.1 Family & People | Chinese | Pinyin | English | sister) | ### 1.2 Food & Drink | Chinese | Pinyin | English | |---------|--------|---------| | 米饭 | **mǐfàn** | rice | | 面条 | **miàntiáo** | noodles | | 包子 | **bāozǐ** | steamed bun | | 饺子 | **jiǎozi** | dumpling | | 鸡蛋 | **jīdàn** | egg | | 牛肉 | **niúròu** | beef | | 猪肉 | **zhūròu** | pork | | 鱼 | **yú** | fish | | 蔬菜 | **shūcài** | vegetables | | 水果 | **shuǐguǒ** | fruit | | 苹果 | **píngguǒ** | apple | | 香蕉 | **xiāngjiāo** | banana | | 橙子 | **chéngzi** | orange | | 西瓜 | **xīguā** | watermelon | | 面包 | **miànbāo** | bread | | 饮料 | **yǐnliào** | beverage | | 茶 | **chá** | tea | | 咖啡 | **kāfēi** | coffee | | 糖 | **táng** | sugar | | 盐 | **yán** | salt | | 酱油 | **jiàngyóu** | soy sauce | | 醋 | **cù** | vinegar | | 辣椒 | **làjiāo** | chili pepper | | 鸡肉 | **jīròu** | chicken meat | | 鸭肉 | **yāròu** | duck meat | | 海鲜 | **hǎixiān** | seafood | | 豆腐 | **dòufu** | tofu | | 豆浆 | **dòujiāng** | soy milk | | 燕麦 | **yànmài** | oats | | 雪糕 | **xuěgāo** | ice cream (cone) | | 冰淇淋 | **bīngqílín** | ice cream (cup) | ### 1.3 Places & Public Spaces | Chinese | Pinyin | English | |---------|--------|---------| | 学校 | **xuéxiào** | school | | 医院 | **yīyuàn** | hospital | | 超市 | **chāoshì** | supermarket | | 公园 | **gōngyuán** | park | | 饭店 | **fàndiàn** | restaurant | | 图书馆 | **túshūguǎn** | library | | 电影院 | **diànyǐngyuàn** | cinema | | 火车站 | **huǒchē zhàn** | train station zhàn** | bus stop | ### 1.4 Everyday Objects | Chinese | Pinyin | English | |---------|--------|---------| | 手机 | **shǒujī** | mobile phone | | 电脑 | **diànnǎo** | computer | | 电视 | **diànshì** | TV | car | | 自行车 | **zìxíngchē** | bicycle | | 公共汽车 | **gōnggòng qìchē** | bus | | 票 | **piào** | ticket | | 车票 | **chē piào** | train/bus ticket | | 门 | **mén** | door | | 窗户 | **chuānghù** | window | | 床 | **chuáng** | bed | | 桌子 | **zhuōzi** | table | | 椅子 | **yǐzi** | chair | | 冰箱 | **bīngxiāng** | refrigerator | | 空调 | **kōngtiáo** | air‑conditioner | | 洗衣机 | **xǐyījī** | washing machine | > **Tip:** When you meet a new noun, say it aloud three times, focusing on the tone marks you practiced in Module 1. Record yourself and compare to a native speaker if possible. --- ## 2. Measure Words: The “Counting Units” of Chinese In English we simply add “-s” or use “a”/“an”. Chinese, however, requires a **measure word** (sometimes called a **classifier**) between the number and the noun. The measure word conveys the shape, function, or category of the object being counted. ### 2.1 Why Measure Words Matter - **Clarity** – “三**本**书” (three **books**) tells the listener you are counting bound items. - **Politeness** – Using the respectful classifier **位** for people shows courtesy, especially in formal contexts. - **Grammar** – The pattern *Number + Measure + Noun* is the backbone of noun phrases you’ll build throughout this book. ### 2.2 Core Measure Words for This Module | Category | Typical Measure Word(s) | Example | Note | |----------|------------------------|---------|------| | **People** | **个** (gè) – generic, informal
**位** (wèi) – polite, formal | **三位老师** (sān wèi lǎoshī) – three teachers (respectful) | Use **位** when addressing elders, teachers, or in a business setting. | | **Flat Objects** | **张** (zhāng) – sheets, tickets, photos, tables, beds | **两张票** (liǎng zhāng piào) – two tickets | Think of “flat” as “surface area”. | | **Long, Thin, Flexible Items** | **条** (tiáo) – ropes, pants, fish, roads, rivers | **五条河** (wǔ tiáo hé) – five rivers | **条** also works for **snacks** like **一条面包** (a stick of bread). | | **Bound/Stackable Items** | **本** (běn) – books, magazines, notebooks | **四本杂志** (sì běn zázhì) – four magazines | *本* emphasizes the “pages” aspect. | | **Containers for Liquids** | **杯** (bēi) – cups, glasses, mugs | **三杯咖啡** (sān bēi kāfēi) – three cups of coffee | Use **瓶** (píng) for bottles, **壶** (hú) for kettles. | | **Small Animals** | **只** (zhī) – birds, cats, dogs, insects | **两只鸟** (liǎng zhī niǎo) – two birds | **只** is also a general classifier for many single items. | | **Vehicles** | **辆** (liàng) – cars, bicycles, buses | **一辆自行车** (yī liàng zìxíngchē) – one bicycle | **部** (bù) is used for larger machines (e.g., **一部手机**). | > **Reminder:** The numbers you learned in Module 3 (一 yī, 二 èr, 三 sān, …) always come **before** the measure word, never after it. ### 2.3 Quick Check: Choose the Right Measure Word | Noun | Correct Measure Word | Reason | |------|----------------------|--------| | 老师 (teacher) | **位** or **个** | People; **位** is more polite | | 票 (ticket) | **张** | Flat object | | 面条 (noodles) | **碗** (bowl) / **条** (if referring to a strand) | Long, flexible; **碗** when counting servings | | 书 (book) | **本** | Bound pages | | 电脑 (computer) | **台** (tái) – not covered here, but **部** also works | Large machine; note for later modules | --- ## 3. Building Simple Noun Phrases Now that you have the nouns and measure words, you can combine them with numbers to form **noun phrases**. The pattern is: ``` Number + Measure Word + Noun ``` ### 3.1 Using Numbers from Module 3 Recall the basic numbers (1–10) and the special form **两** (liǎng) for “two” when it appears before a measure word. | Number | Pinyin | Example Phrase | |--------|--------|----------------| | 一 | yī | **一本书** (yī běn shū) – one book | | 两 | liǎng | **两杯水** (liǎng bēi shuǐ) – two glasses of water | | 三 | sān | **三张票** (sān zhāng piào) – three tickets | | 四 | sì | **四条鱼** (sì tiáo yú) – four fish | | 五 | wǔ | **五位老师** (wǔ wèi lǎoshī) – five teachers | | … | … | … | ### 3.2 Practice Set 1 – Fill in the Blanks 1. ___ (three) **本** 书 → **___** 2. ___ (two) **位** 同学 → **___** 3. ___ (five) **张** 照片 → **___** 4. ___ (one) **条** 裙子 → **___** 5. ___ (four) **杯** 茶 → **___** *Answers:* 1. **三本书** 2. **两位同学** 3. **五张照片** 4. **一条裙子** 5. **四杯茶** ### 3.3 Combining Nouns with Adjectives Chinese adjectives usually **precede** the noun, and the measure word stays after the number. The basic order is: ``` Number + Measure Word + Adjective + Noun ``` > **Example:** *两杯**热**水* (liǎng bēi rè shuǐ) – two cups of **hot** water. #### Common Descriptive Adjectives | Adjective | Pinyin | English | |-----------|--------|---------| | 大 | dà | big | | 小 | xiǎo | small | | 好 | hǎo | good | | 坏 | huài | bad | | 甜 | tián | sweet | | 辣 | là | spicy | | 热 | rè | hot | | 冷 | lěng | cold | | 漂亮 | piàoliang | beautiful | | 便宜 | piányí | cheap | #### Example Sentences | Phrase | English | |--------|---------| | **三本** **新** **书** | three **new** books | | **两位** **年长** **老师** | two **elderly** teachers | | **四张** **彩色** **照片** | four **colorful** photos | | **一条** **长** **面条** | one **long** noodle | | **五杯** **冷** **饮料** | five **cold** drinks | > **Tip:** When an adjective modifies a noun that already has a measure word, the adjective still goes **before** the noun, not before the measure word. Think of the measure word as a “container” for the counted item. ### 3.4 Practice Set 2 – Build the Phrase Create a phrase using the number, appropriate measure word, an adjective from the list above, and the noun. 1. (four) **张** *blue* **纸** → ___ 2. (one) **位** *friendly* **医生** → ___ 3. (two) **本** *interesting* **杂志** → ___ 4. (three) **杯** *cold* **啤酒** → ___ 5. (five) **条** *thin* **鱼** → ___ *Suggested Answers:* 1. **四张蓝纸** (sì zhāng lán zhǐ) – four sheets of blue paper 2. **一位友好的医生** (yī wèi yǒuhǎo de yīshēng) – one friendly doctor 3. **两本有趣的杂志** (liǎng běn yǒuqù de zázhì) – two interesting magazines 4. **三杯冷啤酒** (sān bēi lěng píjiǔ) – three cups of cold beer 5. **五条细鱼** (wǔ tiáo xì yú) – five thin fish --- ## 4. Pronunciation Checklist for New Nouns and Measure Words Even if the characters are correct, mis‑pronouncing a tone can change the meaning entirely. Follow these steps each time you add a new word to your mental inventory: 1. **Identify the tone** (1st‑4th) using the tone marks already familiar from Module 1. 2. **Say the syllable slowly**, checking that the pitch contour matches the tone. 3. **Link the syllable to the next one** (e.g., *liǎng zhāng*) while maintaining tone integrity. 4. **Record** a short clip and compare it to a native speaker (YouTube, Pleco, or a language exchange partner). > **Common Pitfalls** - **个 (gè)** is a 4th‑tone “falling” syllable; avoid turning it into a neutral tone. - **位 (wèi)** also carries a 4th tone – keep the “sharp” drop. - **张 (zhāng)** has a 1st tone; it should stay high and level, even when spoken quickly. --- ## 5. Interactive Mini‑Dialogue Practice the new vocabulary in a short, realistic exchange. Read each line aloud, paying attention to the measure words. > **A:** 你好！请问你要几**杯**咖啡？ (Nǐhǎo! Qǐngwèn nǐ yào jǐ bēi kāfēi?) – *Hello! How many cups of coffee would you like?* > **B:** 我要**两杯**咖啡，**一杯**热的，**一杯**冰的。 (Wǒ yào liǎng bēi kāfēi, yī bēi rè de, yī bēi bīng de.) – *I’d like two cups: one hot, one iced.* > **A:** 好的。还有**三本** **中文** **书** 吗？ (Hǎo de. Hái yǒu sān běn zhōngwén shū ma?) – *Okay. Do you also need three Chinese books?* > **B:** 不需要，谢谢。请给我**两位** **服务员** 的**名片**。 (Bù xūyào, xièxiè. Qǐng gěi wǒ liǎng wèi fúwùyuán de míngpiàn.) – *No, thank you. Please give me the business cards of two waiters.* Notice how the measure words **杯**, **本**, and **位** appear exactly where the numbers sit. --- ## 6. Consolidation Activities ### 6.1 Matching Game Match each noun to its most common measure word. | Noun | Measure Word | |------|--------------| | 书 | ? | | 票 | ? | | 河 | ? | | 老师 | ? | | 电脑 | ? | | 鱼 | ? | | 照片 | ? | | 面条 (serving) | ? | | 车 | ? | | 眼镜 | ? | *Answers:* 书‑本, 票‑张, 河‑条, 老师‑位/个, 电脑‑台 (or 部), 鱼‑条, 照片‑张, 面条‑碗 (or 条), 车‑辆, 眼镜‑副. ### 6.2 Fill‑in‑the‑Blank Paragraph Read the paragraph and insert the correct **number + measure word** combination. > 昨天我去**___** (three) **___** (school) 看**___** (two) **___** (teacher). 我们一起喝了**___** (one) **___** (cup) **热** (hot) **茶**，然后买了**___** (four) **___** (book) **新** (new) **的** **中文** **教材**。回家的路上，我看到**___** (five) **___** (dog) 在公园里跑。 *Suggested Completion:* > 昨天我去**三所学校** 看**两位老师**。我们一起喝了**一杯热茶**，然后买了**四本新中文教材**。回家的路上，我看到**五只狗** 在公园里跑。 --- ## 7. Summary of Core Points - **Measure words** sit between numbers and nouns; they reflect the shape or category of the counted item. - **People**: use **个** (informal) or **位** (polite). - **Flat objects**: **张** (e.g., tickets, photos). - **Long, thin items**: **条** (e.g., fish, roads). - Build noun phrases with the pattern **Number + Measure + Noun**; add adjectives **before** the noun. - Practice pronunciation of each new syllable, respecting the tones you already mastered. --- ## Key Takeaways - **80 high‑frequency nouns** are now in your toolkit; review them regularly and say each aloud three times. - **Measure words** are essential for natural Chinese; remember **个/位**, **张**, and **条** as the three most common classifiers for people, flat objects, and long objects. - Forming a noun phrase follows a simple, repeatable pattern: **Number + Measure Word + (Noun with optional adjective)**. - Use the polite classifier **位** when talking to or about teachers, elders, or in formal settings. - Consistent pronunciation practice—checking tones, linking syllables, and recording yourself—will cement both the words and the classifiers. Proceed to the next module when you feel comfortable counting and describing everyday items. Mastery of nouns and measure words will make every subsequent conversation smoother and more accurate. Happy learning!

modules.title: Module 5: Simple Sentence Structures and Question Forms
modules.content:
## 让我们开口说句子——从“我吃苹果”到“他什么时候来？”  

想象你在北京的咖啡店，服务员把菜单递给你。你想说：**“我想要一杯咖啡。”**  
如果只会说 **“咖啡”**，对话就卡住了。这个章节教你把 **主语‑动词‑宾语 (S‑V‑O)** 的基本句子拼起来，并把它们变成各种常用问题。只要掌握下面的几条规则，你就能在日常情境里自如表达和提问。

---

## 1. 主语‑动词‑宾语 (S‑V‑O)——中文的基本句型  

中文的核心句子结构是 **主语‑动词‑宾语**，类似英文的 “I eat apple”。  
- **主语 (Subject)**：说话的“谁”或“什么”。  
- **动词 (Verb)**：动作或状态。  
- **宾语 (Object)**：动词作用的对象。  

### 1.1 结构示例  

| 中文句子 | 拼音 | 英文直译 |
|----------|------|----------|
| 我吃苹果。 | wǒ chī píngguǒ. | I eat apple. |
| 小李喝茶。 | xiǎo lǐ hē chá. | Xiao Li drinks tea. |
| 他们看电影。 | tāmen kàn diànyǐng. | They watch a movie. |

> **Tip:** 句子结尾的句号（。）在口语中通常省略，口气自然时直接停顿即可。

### 1.2 位置自由度  

在 S‑V‑O 结构里，**动词**永远位于 **主语** 之后，**宾语** 紧随动词。  
这与英语的 **S‑V‑O** 完全对应，学习起来没有额外的语序负担。  

---

## 2. 肯定句的常用动词  

在本模块我们只需掌握几个最常用的动词，它们在日常对话里出现频率极高：

| 动词 | 拼音 | 常见搭配（宾语） |
|------|------|----------------|
| 是 | shì | 是老师、是北京人 |
| 有 | yǒu | 有时间、有钱 |
| 在 | zài | 在学校、在北京 |
| 吃 | chī | 吃饭、吃水果 |
| 喝 | hē | 喝水、喝咖啡 |
| 看 | kàn | 看电影、看书 |
| 去 | qù | 去商店、去北京 |

> **Note:** “是”后面常跟 **名词**（而不是动词），因此它的结构是 **S‑是‑N**，但仍然属于“肯定句”范畴，后面章节会专门讲。

### 2.1 示例练习  

1. **我 + 是 + 学生** → **我是学生。** (wǒ shì xuéshēng)  
2. **她 + 有 + 朋友** → **她有朋友。** (tā yǒu péngyǒu)  
3. **我们 + 去 + 超市** → **我们去超市。** (wǒmen qù chāoshì)

---

## 3. 把肯定句变成 **是‑吗** 的疑问句  

### 3.1 “吗” 的作用  

**吗 (ma)** 是一个 **疑问语气助词**，放在陈述句末尾即可把句子变成 **是非（yes/no）** 疑问句。它本身不改变词序，只是让听者知道你在提问。

### 3.2 形成步骤  

1. **先写出完整的肯定句**（S‑V‑O）。  
2. **在句子末尾加上 “吗”。**  

#### 示例  

| 肯定句 | 加 “吗” 后 | 拼音 |
|--------|-----------|------|
| 你吃饭。 | 你吃饭吗？ | nǐ chī fàn ma? |
| 他有车。 | 他有车吗？ | tā yǒu chē ma? |
| 我们去图书馆。 | 我们去图书馆吗？ | wǒmen qù túshūguǎn ma? |

> **Tip:** 语调上扬（像英文的上升调）帮助对方辨认这是一个问题。

### 3.3 常见错误提醒  

- **不要把 “吗” 放在动词前**：*错* → “吗你吃饭？”  
- **不要省略句子中的必要成分**：如果原句缺了宾语，疑问句也会不完整。  

---

## 4. 用 “什么、哪里、谁、几时” 提出 **wh‑questions**  

### 4.1 什么 (shénme) – 询问事物  

**结构**：**S‑V‑什么**（或 **什么‑V‑S** 视动词而定）  
- **我想吃什么？** (wǒ xiǎng chī shénme?) – “我想吃**什么**？”  
- **他买了什么？** (tā mǎi le shénme?) – “他买了**什么**？”  

### 4.2 哪里 (nǎlǐ) – 询问地点  

**结构**：**S‑V‑哪里** 或 **哪里‑V‑S**（常用于 “在”）  
- **我们去哪里？** (wǒmen qù nǎlǐ?) – “我们去**哪里**？”  
- **他在北京哪里？** (tā zài Běijīng nǎlǐ?) – “他在北京**哪里**？”  

### 4.3 谁 (shéi) – 询问人  

**结构**：**S‑V‑谁** 或 **谁‑V‑S**（尤其是 “是”）  
- **谁在敲门？** (shéi zài qiāo mén?) – “**谁**在敲门？”  
- **这是谁的书？** (zhè shì shéi de shū?) – “**这**是**谁**的书？”  

### 4.4 几时 (jǐshí) – 询问时间  

**结构**：**S‑V‑几时** 或 **几时‑V‑S**（常与 “在” 连用）  
- **我们几时见面？** (wǒmen jǐshí jiànmiàn?) – “**我们****几时**见面？”  
- **火车几时到？** (huǒchē jǐshí dào?) – “**火车****几时**到？”  

### 4.5 练习：把下面的肯定句改成 wh‑question  

1. **我买了水果。** → **我买了什么？**  
2. **他住在北京。** → **他住在哪里？**  
3. **老师在教室。** → **老师在哪里？**  
4. **她明天来。** → **她几时来？**  

> **Note:** “几时” 在口语里常被 **什么时候 (shénme shíhòu)** 取代，两者意义相同，只是语体略有差别。  

---

## 5. 否定句：用 **不** 与 **没**  

中文否定有两大类：**状态/习惯的否定** 用 **不 (bù)**，**已经发生的动作或存在的否定** 用 **没 (méi)**。  

### 5.1 “不” 的使用规则  

| 用法 | 说明 | 示例 |
|------|------|------|
| **动词** 前 | 表示“不是、不要、不会”。 | **我不吃肉。** (wǒ bù chī ròu) |
| **形容词** 前 | 表示“不是”。 | **天气不热。** (tiānqì bù rè) |
| **习惯** | 用于表示经常不做的事。 | **他不喝咖啡。** (tā bù hē kāfēi) |

> **Tip:** “不” 的声调在四声前会变成 **轻声** (bù → bu˙)，如 **不吃**。  

### 5.2 “没” 的使用规则  

| 用法 | 说明 | 示例 |
|------|------|------|
| **动词** 前（过去或将来） | 表示“没有”。 | **我没去北京。** (wǒ méi qù Běijīng) |
| **有** 前 | 否定“有”。 | **我没有钱。** (wǒ méiyǒu qián) |
| **完成时** | 与 “了” 连用，表示未完成。 | **我没吃** (wǒ méi chī) – “我还没吃”。 |

> **Note:** “没” 只能用于 **有/在/去/来** 等动词，不能直接放在形容词前（如 *“没热”* 是错误的）。  

### 5.3 对比练习  

| 肯定句 | 否定（不） | 否定（没） |
|--------|------------|------------|
| 我喝茶。 | 我**不**喝茶。 | 我**没**喝茶。 |
| 他去图书馆。 | 他**不**去图书馆。 | 他**没**去图书馆。 |
| 我有时间。 | (不适用) | 我**没有**时间。 |

> **Why both exist?**  
> - **不** 表示 **意愿或习惯**（我不想喝）  
> - **没** 表示 **事实上的缺失**（我没买）  

---

## 6. 综合练习：从肯定句到疑问句，再到否定句  

> **情境**：你在北京的地铁站，想了解下一班车的时间、目的地以及是否拥挤。请用本章所学完成以下对话。  

| 步骤 | 目标 | 示例答案 |
|------|------|----------|
| 1 | 陈述你现在的状态 | **我在地铁站。** (wǒ zài dìtiě zhàn) |
| 2 | 用 **吗** 提问是否有下一班车 | **还有下一班车吗？** (hái yǒu xià yī bān chē ma?) |
| 3 | 用 **几时** 询问发车时间 | **下一班车几时出发？** (xià yī bān chē jǐshí chūfā?) |
| 4 | 用 **哪里** 询问终点站 | **下一班车去哪里？** (xià yī bān chē qù nǎlǐ?) |
| 5 | 用 **不** 表示你不想拥挤 | **我不想拥挤。** (wǒ bù xiǎng yōngjǐ) |
| 6 | 用 **没** 表示你还没买票 | **我没买票。** (wǒ méi mǎi piào) |

把这些句子连起来，你会得到一段自然、完整的对话。练习时先说慢一点，注意 **声调**（参考 Module 1），随后逐步加快语速。

---

## 7. 常见错误速查表  

| 错误类型 | 正确做法 | 例子 |
|----------|----------|------|
| 把 **吗** 放在句首或动词前 | **句末** 加 **吗** | ❌ **吗你吃饭？** → ✅ **你吃饭吗？** |
| 用 **不** 否定已经发生的动作 | 用 **没** | ❌ **我不去北京**（表示不想去） → ✅ **我没去北京**（表示没去过） |
| 省略 **宾语** 导致句子不完整 | 确保动词后有明确宾语 | ❌ **我吃** → ✅ **我吃饭** |
| 在 **谁** 前加 **的** | **谁** 本身是疑问代词，不需要 **的** | ❌ **的谁** → ✅ **谁** |
| 把 **什么** 放在动词后导致语序错误 | 常规 S‑V‑什么，或 **什么‑V‑S**（如 “是什么”） | ❌ **我什么吃** → ✅ **我吃什么** |

---

## 8. 小结练习：自行造句  

请在空格里填入适当的词或助词，使句子完整并符合要求。  

1. (肯定) ___ (我) ___ (喝) ___ (咖啡)。  
2. (是‑吗) ___ (他) ___ (是) ___ (老师) ___？  
3. (什么) ___ (你) ___ (想) ___ ___？  
4. (哪里) ___ (他们) ___ (去) ___？  
5. (不) ___ (我们) ___ (去) ___ (电影院)。  
6. (没) ___ (她) ___ (买) ___ (票)。  

**答案**（供自检）  

1. 我 **喝** 咖啡。  
2. 他 **是** 老师 **吗**？  
3. 你 **想** 什么？  
4. 他们 **去** 哪里？  
5. 我们 **不** 去 电影院。  
6. 她 **没** 买 票。  

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **S‑V‑O** 是中文最基本的句子结构，主语‑动词‑宾语的顺序永不改变。  
- **吗** 只需放在完整陈述句末尾，即可把句子变成 **是‑否** 疑问句。  
- **什么、哪里、谁、几时** 分别对应 **what, where, who, when**，可直接置于动词后形成 **wh‑questions**。  
- 否定时：**不** 用于表示习惯、意愿或形容词的否定；**没** 用于已经发生的动作或“有/在/去/来”等动词的否定。  
- 练习时先写出肯定句，再依次加上 **吗**、**wh‑词**、**不/没**，检验语序和助词位置是否正确。  

掌握了这些句型，你已经可以在日常生活中自信地说出 **“我吃苹果。”**、**“你喝茶吗？”**、**“他是谁？”** 与 **“我们不去超市。”** 等句子。下一步，继续学习 **常用动词** 与 **表达需求**，让你的中文对话更丰富、更自然。

modules.title: Module 6: Common Verbs and Expressing Needs
modules.content:
## 1. Why “I want a coffee” is the perfect starter sentence  

Imagine you are sitting in a bustling Shanghai café. The barista says, “请问您想要点什么？” (Qǐngwèn nín **xiǎng yào** diǎn shénme?) – “May I ask what you would like to order?”  
Your reply can be as simple as **“我要一杯咖啡。”** (Wǒ **yào** yì bēi kāfēi.) – “I want a cup of coffee.”  

That one short exchange already contains three of the core verbs we will master in this chapter: **想**, **要**, and **可以**.  By the end of the next sections you will be able to:

* State what you **want** or **need** (想, 要)  
* Ask for **permission** or **possibility** (可以, 能, 会)  
* Combine verbs with objects to make polite requests  
* Turn any of those sentences into a negative form (我不想去, 我不能喝…)  

Let’s break each verb down, see how they behave in a sentence, and practice the patterns you’ll use every day.

---

## 2. The “wish” verb – **想 (xiǎng)**  

### 2.1 Basic pattern  

```
Subject + 想 + Verb/Activity + (Object)
```

| English | Chinese (pinyin) | Literal |
|---------|------------------|---------|
| I want to go | 我想去 (Wǒ xiǎng qù) | I want to go |
| She wants to eat | 她想吃饭 (Tā xiǎng chī fàn) | She wants to eat |
| We want to watch a movie | 我们想看电影 (Wǒmen xiǎng kàn diànyǐng) | We want to watch a movie |

> **Tip:** When **想** is followed by another verb, the second verb stays in its base form; no “to” is added in Chinese.

### 2.2 Adding an object  

If the object is a **noun phrase**, place it after the verb:

* 我想喝 **咖啡**。 (Wǒ xiǎng hē kāfēi.) – “I want to drink coffee.”  
* 他们想买 **一本书**。 (Tāmen xiǎng mǎi yì běn shū.) – “They want to buy a book.”

### 2.3 Negative form  

To say you **don’t want** to do something, insert **不** before the verb that follows **想**:

* 我不想去。 (Wǒ **bù** xiǎng qù.) – “I don’t want to go.”  
* 她不想吃辣的。 (Tā **bù** xiǎng chī là de.) – “She doesn’t want to eat spicy food.”

---

## 3. The “need / demand” verb – **要 (yào)**  

### 3.1 Direct request  

```
Subject + 要 + MeasureWord + Noun
```

| English | Chinese (pinyin) |
|---------|------------------|
| I want a cup of tea | 我要一杯茶 (Wǒ yào yì bēi chá) |
| He needs a new phone | 他要一部新手机 (Tā yào yì bù xīn shǒujī) |
| We want two tickets | 我们要两张票 (Wǒmen yào liǎng zhāng piào) |

> **Note:** The **measure word** (杯, 部, 张) is mandatory in Chinese when counting nouns. Review Module 4 if you need a refresher.

### 3.2 Combining **要** with a verb  

When the object is an action rather than a concrete noun, **要** can be followed by a verb phrase:

* 我**要**去北京。 (Wǒ yào qù Běijīng.) – “I need to go to Beijing.”  
* 他们**要**学习汉语。 (Tāmen yào xuéxí Hànyǔ.) – “They want to study Chinese.”

### 3.3 Polite request with **请**  

Adding **请** (qǐng – “please”) before **要** makes the request softer:

* 请给我**要**一杯水。 (Qǐng gěi wǒ yào yì bēi shuǐ.) – “Please give me a cup of water.”  

### 3.4 Negative form  

Place **不** before **要**:

* 我**不要**喝酒。 (Wǒ **bù yào** hē jiǔ.) – “I don’t want to drink alcohol.”  
* 他**不要**买这个。 (Tā **bù yào** mǎi zhè ge.) – “He doesn’t want to buy this.”

---

## 4. Permission and possibility – **可以 (kěyǐ)** & **能 (néng)**  

### 4.1 Asking for permission with **可以**  

```
Subject + 可以 + Verb + (Object)?
```

* 我可以坐这里吗？ (Wǒ kěyǐ zuò zhèlǐ ma?) – “May I sit here?”  
* 你可以帮我吗？ (Nǐ kěyǐ bāng wǒ ma?) – “Can you help me?”

### 4.2 Expressing ability with **能**  

```
Subject + 能 + Verb + (Object)?
```

* 我能说一点中文。 (Wǒ néng shuō yìdiǎn Zhōngwén.) – “I can speak a little Chinese.”  
* 她能开车去公司。 (Tā néng kāichē qù gōngsī.) – “She can drive to the office.”

### 4.3 The subtle difference  

| Verb | Typical use | Example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| **可以** | Permission / possibility | 这里**可以**抽烟吗？ (Is it allowed to smoke here?) |
| **能** | Physical or learned ability | 我**能**跑五公里。 (I can run five kilometers.) |

> **Tip:** In many everyday situations the two are interchangeable, but the nuance matters when you want to stress *permission* (可以) versus *capability* (能).

### 4.4 Negative forms  

* **不可以** – “not allowed / cannot”  
  * 这里**不可以**吃东西。 (Zhèlǐ bù kěyǐ chī dōngxi.) – “You can’t eat here.”  

* **不能** – “cannot / be unable to”  
  * 我**不能**今天去。 (Wǒ bù néng jīntiān qù.) – “I cannot go today.”  

---

## 5. The “know how to / will be able to” verb – **会 (huì)**  

### 5.1 Expressing learned skill  

```
Subject + 会 + Verb
```

* 我**会**做饭。 (Wǒ huì zuò fàn.) – “I can cook.”  
* 他**会**弹吉他。 (Tā huì tán jítā.) – “He can play the guitar.”  

### 5.2 Future possibility (similar to “will”)  

When combined with a time word, **会** also indicates a future event:

* 明天我**会**去上海。 (Míngtiān wǒ huì qù Shànghǎi.) – “Tomorrow I will go to Shanghai.”  

### 5.3 Negative form  

* 我**不会**游泳。 (Wǒ **bù huì** yóuyǒng.) – “I can’t swim.”  

---

## 6. Putting verbs together – “verb + object” request patterns  

### 6.1 The “verb‑object” construction  

Chinese often places the **object** directly after the **verb** without prepositions:

* 我要**一杯咖啡**。 (Wǒ yào yì bēi kāfēi.) – “I want a cup of coffee.”  
* 请**给我**一张票。 (Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhāng piào.) – “Please give me a ticket.”  

### 6.2 Layered requests  

You can stack two verbs to convey a more nuanced request:

* 我**想****要**一本词典。 (Wǒ xiǎng yào yì běn cídiǎn.) – “I would like to have a dictionary.”  
* 你**可以****帮**我**买**这个吗？ (Nǐ kěyǐ bāng wǒ mǎi zhè ge ma?) – “Can you help me buy this?”

### 6.3 Practice drill  

1. **Fill‑in the blank** – Write a sentence using the given verb and object.  

   * Verb: **想** Object: **一份午餐**  
   * Answer: 我**想**一份午餐。 (Wǒ xiǎng yí fèn wǔcān.)  

2. **Turn it negative** – Convert the sentence you just created into its negative form.  

   * Answer: 我**不想**一份午餐。 (Wǒ **bù xiǎng** yí fèn wǔcān.)

---

## 7. Quick‑fire conversation practice  

Below is a short dialogue that strings together everything covered so far. Read it aloud, mimic the intonation you learned in Module 1, and then try to swap the roles.

> **服务员**：请问您**想**要点什么？  
> **你**：我**要**一杯**咖啡**，请**给**我**加**一点**牛奶**。  
> **服务员**：可以**加**吗？  
> **你**：可以。  
> **服务员**：您**会**喝**热**还是**凉**的？  
> **你**：我**不想**喝**热**的，**要**凉的。  

*Key structures highlighted:* 想 + verb, 要 + measure‑word + noun, 可以 + verb, 会 + verb, 不想 + verb.

---

## 8. Common pitfalls for beginners  

| Pitfall | Why it happens | Correct pattern |
|---------|----------------|-----------------|
| Using **要** without a measure word | Learners forget the noun‑counting rule from Module 4 | 我要**一**杯**水** (not *我要杯水*) |
| Mixing up **可以** and **能** for ability | Both translate to “can,” but the nuance is different | **能**跑，**可以**抽烟 |
| Forgetting the negative **不** before the verb (e.g., *我不想去* → *我想不去*) | Chinese places **不** before the verb, not after | Correct: **我不想去** |
| Adding “to” in English after **想** or **要** (e.g., *我想**去** to Beijing*) | Chinese does not use “to” after these verbs | Correct: **我想去北京** |

---

## 9. Mini‑exercises for mastery  

### 9.1 Translation challenge  

Translate the following English sentences into Chinese. Use the verb highlighted in bold.

1. **Want**: I want two tickets.  
2. **Can (permission)**: May I open the window?  
3. **Can (ability)**: She can play the piano.  
4. **Know how**: We will be able to finish tomorrow.  
5. **Don’t want**: He doesn’t want to study tonight.

### 9.2 Fill‑in‑the‑blank  

Complete each sentence with the appropriate verb (**想 / 要 / 可以 / 能 / 会**) and any necessary measure words.

1. 我 ___ 一杯茶。  
2. 她 ___ 说中文。  
3. 你 ___ (permission) ___ 进来吗？  
4. 我 ___ (ability) ___ 游泳。  
5. 我 ___ (negative) ___ 去电影院。  

*Answers are provided at the end of the book for self‑check.*

---

## 10. Bringing it all together – a real‑life scenario  

You’re traveling in Chengdu and need a taxi, a hotel reservation, and a recommendation for lunch. Using the verbs you’ve just mastered, you might say:

1. **Taxi**: 对不起，我**想**叫一辆**出租车**。  
2. **Hotel**: 我**要**一个**双人间**，请**给**我**看**一下房间。  
3. **Lunch**: 这里**可以****吃**什么好吃的？  

Notice how each request follows the patterns we practiced: **想 + verb**, **要 + measure‑word + noun**, **可以 + verb**.

---

## Key Takeaways  

* **想** expresses a wish or desire; use **不想** for the negative.  
* **要** is the go‑to verb for “need / want” a concrete object; always include the correct **measure word**.  
* **可以** asks for permission or indicates possibility; **不可以** means “not allowed.”  
* **能** focuses on *ability*; its negative is **不能**.  
* **会** conveys learned skill (“can”) or future likelihood (“will”).  
* Combine verbs with objects directly (verb‑object construction) to make polite requests.  
* Negative forms always place **不** before the verb you are negating.  

With these building blocks, you can confidently state what you want, ask for permission, and describe what you’re able to do—essential skills for everyday Chinese conversation. Keep practicing the drills, and soon the patterns will feel as natural as the greetings you learned in Module 2. Happy speaking!

modules.title: Module 7: Asking for Directions and Transportation
modules.content:
## 1️⃣  A QUICK SCENARIO  
You’re in Shanghai for the first time. After a morning of sightseeing, you decide to visit the **Shanghai Museum**. You pull out your phone, type “上海博物馆” and realize you have no idea how to get there. A passer‑by smiles and says, “**往这边走**，左拐再右转。”  
In the next few minutes you will be able to (1) ask *where* something is, (2) request *how* to get there, (3) understand the basic left‑right‑front‑back vocabulary, and (4) talk about the bus, subway, taxi, or walking options that get you there.

---

## 2️⃣  Asking for Directions  

### 2.1  Core Question Patterns  

| English | Chinese (pinyin) | When to use |
|---------|------------------|-------------|
| Where is …? | **… 在哪里？** (*… zài nǎ lǐ?*) | General location inquiry |
| How do I get to …? | **… 怎么走？** (*… zěn me zǒu?*) | Asking for a route or method |
| Is it far? | **远吗？** (*yuǎn ma?*) | Follow‑up after the first answer |
| Is it near …? | **离 … 近吗？** (*lí … jìn ma?*) | Comparing distances |

> **Tip:** The particle **吗** turns a statement into a yes/no question. You already met this in Module 5.

### 2.2  Example Dialogues  

1. **At a hotel lobby**  

| Speaker | Dialogue | Pinyin |
|--------|----------|--------|
| You | 请问，**地铁站**在哪里？ | Qǐng wèn, dì tiě zhàn zài nǎ lǐ? |
| Receptionist | 在前面左边的拐角。 | Zài qián miàn zuǒ biān de guǎi jiǎo. |
| You | 谢谢！**怎么走**？ | Xiè xiè! Zěn me zǒu? |
| Receptionist | 出门往右走，走两百米后左拐。 | Chū mén wǎng yòu zǒu, zǒu liǎng bǎi mǐ hòu zuǒ guǎi. |

2. **On the street**  

| Speaker | Dialogue | Pinyin |
|--------|----------|--------|
| You | 请问，**上海博物馆**怎么走？ | Qǐng wèn, Shànghǎi Bówùguǎn zěn me zǒu? |
| Local | 往前走到第二个红绿灯，左转，然后直走五分钟。 | Wǎng qián zǒu dào dì èr gè hóng lǜ dēng, zuǒ zhuǎn, ránhòu zhí zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng. |

### 2.3  Practice Prompt  

Fill in the blanks with the correct question word (在哪里 / 怎么走 / 远吗).  

1. **北京火车站** ___？  
2. **机场** ___？  
3. 那个咖啡店 ___？  

*(Answers: 1. 在哪里, 2. 怎么走, 3. 远吗)*  

---

## 3️⃣  Directional Vocabulary  

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---------|--------|---------|
| **左** | zuǒ | left |
| **右** | yòu | right |
| **前** | qián | front / ahead |
| **后** | hòu | back / behind |
| **上** | shàng | up / above |
| **下** | xià | down / below |
| **近** | jìn | near |
| **远** | yuǎn | far |
| **拐弯** | guǎi wān | turn (a corner) |
| **直走** | zhí zǒu | go straight |
| **沿着** | yán zhe | along |

### 3.1  Putting Directions Together  

1. **左拐** – turn left  
2. **右转** – turn right  
3. **直走** – go straight ahead  
4. **往前走** – walk forward  
5. **往后走** – walk backward (rarely needed)  

**Sentence pattern:**  
`[起点] + 往 + [方向] + 走 + [距离/时间] + (然后) + [动作]`  

*Example:* “从这里**往左走**两百米**然后右拐**。”  
*(From here, walk left 200 m, then turn right.)*

---

## 4️⃣  Talking About Transportation  

### 4.1  Common Modes & Key Verbs  

| Mode | Chinese | Verb(s) |
|------|---------|---------|
| Bus | **公交车** / **巴士** | **坐** (zuò) – “to ride” |
| Subway | **地铁** | **乘** (chéng) – formal “to take” |
| Taxi | **出租车** | **打车** (dǎ chē) – “to hail a taxi” |
| Walking | **走路** / **步行** | **走** (zǒu) – “to walk” |
| Bicycle (shared) | **共享单车** | **骑** (qí) – “to ride a bike” |

### 4.2  Sample Sentences  

1. **公交** – “我**坐** 322 **路** 去公司。”  
   *Wǒ zuò 322 lù qù gōngsī.* – I take bus 322 to work.  

2. **地铁** – “**乘** 1 号线到**人民广场**站。”  
   *Chéng yī hào xiàn dào Rénmín Guǎngchǎng zhàn.* – Take Line 1 to People’s Square station.  

3. **出租车** – “请**打车**去**外滩**，大约二十分钟。”  
   *Qǐng dǎ chē qù Wàitān, dàyuē èrshí fēnzhōng.* – Please hail a taxi to the Bund, about 20 minutes.  

4. **步行** – “我**走路**去**南京东路**，大概十五分钟。”  
   *Wǒ zǒulù qù Nánjīng Dōng Lù, dàyuē shíwǔ fēnzhōng.* – I’ll walk to East Nanjing Road, about 15 minutes.  

### 4.3  Combining Directions & Transport  

> **Dialogue:** You need to get to a museum using the subway.  

| Speaker | Dialogue | Pinyin |
|--------|----------|--------|
| You | 请问，**地铁**怎么走去**上海博物馆**？ | Qǐng wèn, dìtiě zěn me zǒu qù Shànghǎi Bówùguǎn? |
| Staff | 在**人民广场**站**换乘**2号线，**往左**走到**出口**。 | Zài Rénmín Guǎngchǎng zhàn huànchéng 2 hào xiàn, wǎng zuǒ zǒu dào chūkǒu. |
| You | 谢谢！**坐**几站？ | Xièxiè! Zuò jǐ zhàn? |
| Staff | 三站后**下车**，再**直走**五分钟。 | Sān zhàn hòu xià chē, zài zhí zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng. |

---

## 5️⃣  Reading Simple Transit Signs  

| Sign (Chinese) | Pinyin | Typical English Meaning |
|----------------|--------|--------------------------|
| **入口** | rù kǒu | Entrance |
| **出口** | chū kǒu | Exit |
| **换乘** | huàn chéng | Transfer |
| **站** | zhàn | Station |
| **方向** | fāng xiàng | Direction |
| **左** | zuǒ | Left |
| **右** | yòu | Right |
| **上/下** | shàng / xià | Up / Down (elevators, escalators) |
| **公交** | gōng jiāo | Bus |
| **地铁** | dì tiě | Subway |
| **票价** | piào jià | Fare |

### 5.1  Mini‑Reading Exercise  

> **Scenario:** You are standing in a subway station. Identify the correct actions.  

1. The sign reads **左侧入口** – what do you do?  
2. The sign reads **换乘至 3 号线** – what does this mean?  
3. The sign reads **出口在右** – where will you exit?  

*Answers:* 1️⃣ Use the left‑hand entrance. 2️⃣ Transfer to Line 3. 3️⃣ Exit on the right side.

---

## 6️⃣  Role‑Play: From “Lost” to “Arrived”  

**Characters:**  
- **Lǐ Míng** (tourist)  
- **Zhāng Wěi** (local office worker)  

**Goal:** Lǐ Míng must get from the hotel to the **上海科技馆** (Shanghai Science and Technology Museum) using a combination of walking and subway.

| Step | Dialogue (Chinese) | Pinyin | English |
|------|--------------------|--------|---------|
| 1 | **Lǐ Míng:** 请问，**上海科技馆**怎么走？ | Qǐng wèn, Shànghǎi Kējìguǎn zěn me zǒu? | Excuse me, how do I get to the Shanghai Science Museum? |
| 2 | **Zhāng Wěi:** 先**走路**到**人民广场**站，**大约五分钟**。 | Xiān zǒulù dào Rénmín Guǎngchǎng zhàn, dàyuē wǔ fēnzhōng. | Walk to People’s Square station, about five minutes. |
| 3 | **Lǐ Míng:** 好的，**怎么走**？ | Hǎo de, zěn me zǒu? | OK, how do I walk? |
| 4 | **Zhāng Wěi:** 出门**往右**，**直走**到**地铁入口**。 | Chūmén wǎng yòu, zhí zǒu dào dìtiě rùkǒu. | Exit and turn right, go straight to the subway entrance. |
| 5 | **Lǐ Míng:** **坐**几号线？ | Zuò jǐ hào xiàn? | Which line do I take? |
| 6 | **Zhāng Wěi:** **乘** 1 号线**往****浦东**方向，**换乘** 2 号线在**世纪大道**站。 | Chéng yī hào xiàn wǎng Pǔdōng fāngxiàng, huànchéng èr hào xiàn zài Shìjì Dàdào zhàn. | Take Line 1 toward Pudong, transfer to Line 2 at Century Avenue. |
| 7 | **Lǐ Míng:** **下车**后**往左**走，**直走**到**科技馆**。 | Xià chē hòu wǎng zuǒ zhí zǒu dào Kējìguǎn. | After getting off, turn left and walk straight to the museum. |
| 8 | **Zhāng Wěi:** 大约**二十五分钟**全程。祝你玩得开心！ | Dàyuē èrshí wǔ fēnzhōng quánchéng. Zhù nǐ wán de kāixīn! | About 25 minutes total. Have a great time! |

**Practice:** Swap roles and try the dialogue with a partner. Change the destination (e.g., **外滩**, **南京路步行街**) to reinforce the pattern.

---

## 7️⃣  Exercises  

### 7.1  Fill‑in‑the‑Blank  
Complete each sentence with the appropriate directional word or verb.

1. 请问，**地铁站**_____？  
2. 我_____（坐/乘/打车）**公交**去公司。  
3. 从这里_____（左拐/右转/直走）到**人民广场**站。  
4. **公交车**_____（几号）？  
5. **票价**_____（贵/便宜）吗？

### 7.2  Matching – Vocabulary ↔︎ Meaning  

| A | B |
|---|---|
| 1. 左拐 | a. to transfer |
| 2. 换乘 | b. left |
| 3. 打车 | c. to hail a taxi |
| 4. 直走 | d. go straight |
| 5. 远 | e. far |

### 7.3  Translation (English → Chinese)  

1. Where is the nearest subway entrance?  
2. Walk straight for two hundred meters, then turn right.  
3. I’ll take bus number 56 to the museum.  

*(Encourage learners to check their answers against the key provided at the end of the workbook.)*  

---

## 8️⃣  Pronunciation & Tone Check  

All the new words use the **four tones** you mastered in Module 1. Pay special attention to:

- **左** (zuǒ) – third tone  
- **右** (yòu) – fourth tone  
- **换** (huàn) – fourth tone  

Practice with a language partner or a recording app: say the whole sentence, then isolate the tone‑bearing syllable and repeat three times.

---

## ## Key Takeaways  

- **怎么走** asks *how to get somewhere*; **在哪里** asks *where something is*.  
- Core directional words: **左、右、前、后、上、下、直走、拐弯**.  
- Transport verbs: **坐** (bus), **乘** (subway), **打车** (taxi), **走** (walk), **骑** (bike).  
- Simple transit signs (入口, 出口, 换乘, 站) give essential navigation cues.  
- Combining a location question, a route description, and a transport choice lets you move confidently in any Chinese city.  

Practice the dialogues, read the signs, and soon you’ll turn “lost” into “on time” with native‑like ease. Happy travels!

modules.title: Module 8: Shopping and Dining Conversations
modules.content:
## 1.  A DAY IN THE MARKET: Why “多少钱?” Is the Most Useful Question  
Imagine you are strolling through a bustling market in Chengdu. Stalls of fresh fruit, sizzling street‑food carts, and bright‑colored souvenir shops line the lane. You spot a juicy **桃子** (*táo zi* – peach) that looks perfect for a snack. What do you say?  

> **你** (nǐ) **多少钱**?  
> *Nǐ duō shǎo qián?* – “How much is it?”

That simple question unlocks the whole shopping and dining experience. In the sections that follow you will learn:

* How to **ask about price, size, and availability** of any product.  
* How to **order meals**, request **modifications**, and give **feedback**.  
* The essential **payment phrases** you’ll need at a cash register or restaurant counter.  
* Polite **bargaining** expressions and ways to show **gratitude**.

All of the vocabulary builds on the numbers and measure words you mastered in **Module 3** and **Module 4**, so you’ll see those concepts in action again.

---

## 2.  Core Shopping Vocabulary  

| Chinese | Pinyin | English | Note |
|---------|--------|---------|------|
| **多少钱** | duō shǎo qián | how much (price) | “多少钱” literally “how many money”. |
| **多少** | duō shǎo | how many / how much | Use alone when the noun is obvious. |
| **价钱** | jià qián | price (noun) | Often used with **是** (shì) – “price is …”. |
| **尺寸** | chǐ cùn | size / dimension | Common with clothing or shoes. |
| **颜色** | yán sè | color | |
| **有** | yǒu | have / there is | “有吗?” – “Is there …?” |
| **没有** | méi yǒu | don’t have / there isn’t | |
| **可以** | kě yǐ | can / may | Used in permission questions – “Can I …?” |
| **请** | qǐng | please | Polite particle placed before a request. |
| **谢谢** | xiè xie | thank you | |
| **对不起** | duì bu qǐ | sorry / excuse me | Useful when you need to get attention. |
| **打折** | dǎ zhé | discount / to discount | “有打折吗?” – “Is there a discount?” |

> **Tip:** When you see a new noun, attach the appropriate **measure word** (e.g., **个**, **件**, **双**) that you learned in Module 4. Example: **一个** (*yí gè*) for a generic item, **件** (*jiàn*) for clothing, **双** (*shuāng*) for a pair of shoes.

---

## 3.  Asking About Price, Size, and Availability  

### 3.1.  Price‑Related Questions  

1. **这​…​多少钱？**  
   *Zhè … duō shǎo qián?* – “How much is this …?”  

2. **可以便宜一点吗？**  
   *Kě yǐ pián yí yì diǎn ma?* – “Can it be a little cheaper?”  

3. **有折扣吗？**  
   *Yǒu zhě kòu ma?* – “Is there a discount?”  

4. **如果买两件，能打折吗？**  
   *Rú guǒ mǎi liǎng jiàn, néng dǎ zhé ma?* – “If I buy two, can I get a discount?”  

### 3.2.  Size & Color  

| Phrase | Pinyin | Meaning |
|--------|--------|---------|
| **这个​…​有几种颜色？** | zhè ge … yǒu jǐ zhǒng yán sè? | “How many colors does this … have?” |
| **尺寸是多少？** | chǐ cùn shì duō shǎo? | “What is the size?” |
| **有大号/小号吗？** | yǒu dà hào/xiǎo hào ma? | “Do you have a large/small size?” |
| **可以试穿吗？** | kě yǐ shì chuān ma? | “May I try it on?” |

### 3.3.  Availability  

* **还有吗？** – *Hái yǒu ma?* – “Is there any left?”  
* **有现货吗？** – *Yǒu xiàn huò ma?* – “Do you have it in stock?”  
* **什么时候有货？** – *Shén me shí hòu yǒu huò?* – “When will it be available?”  

---

## 4.  Polite Bargaining  

Bargaining is common in markets and small shops, but it is always done with respect. The following patterns let you negotiate without sounding demanding.

| Pattern | Pinyin | English |
|---------|--------|---------|
| **能不能…​** | néng bu néng … | “Can / could you …?” |
| **能不能便宜一点？** | néng bu néng pián yí yì diǎn? | “Could you make it a little cheaper?” |
| **如果我买…​，可以…​吗？** | rú guǒ wǒ mǎi …, kě yǐ … ma? | “If I buy …, may I …?” |
| **谢谢，已经很划算了。** | xiè xie, yǐ jīng hěn huá suàn le. | “Thank you, that’s already a good deal.” |

**Example Dialogue – Bargaining for a Scarf**

> **A:** 这条围巾多少钱？  
> *Zhè tiáo wéi jīn duō shǎo qián?* – “How much is this scarf?”  
> **B:** 五十块。  
> *Wǔ shí kuài.* – “50 yuan.”  
> **A:** 能不能便宜一点？三十块可以吗？  
> *Néng bù néng pián yì diǎn? Sān shí kuài kě yǐ ma?* – “Could you make it cheaper? 30 yuan okay?”  
> **B:** 好的，四十五块。  
> *Hǎo de, sì shí wǔ kuài.* – “Alright, 45 yuan.”  
> **A:** 谢谢！  
> *Xiè xie!* – “Thank you!”

Notice the use of **请** (*qǐng*) is optional in bargaining, but adding it softens the request: **请问能不能…** – “May I ask if you could…”.

---

## 5.  Dining Vocabulary  

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---------|--------|---------|
| **菜单** | cài dān | menu |
| **餐厅** | cān tīng | restaurant |
| **点菜** | diǎn cài | to order dishes |
| **主食** | zhǔ shí | staple food (rice, noodles) |
| **小吃** | xiǎo chī | snack |
| **口味** | kǒu wèi | taste / flavor |
| **辣** | là | spicy |
| **不辣** | bù là | not spicy |
| **加** | jiā | add |
| **少** | shǎo | less |
| **多** | duō | more |
| **不要** | bù yào | don’t want |
| **好吃** | hǎo chī | delicious |
| **不好吃** | bù hǎo chī | not tasty |
| **服务员** | fú wù yuán | waiter / waitress |
| **结账** | jié zhàng | to pay the bill |

---

## 6.  Ordering Meals & Requesting Modifications  

### 6.1.  Getting the Menu and Calling the Waiter  

* **请给我菜单。** – *Qǐng gěi wǒ cài dān.* – “Please give me the menu.”  
* **服务员，点菜。** – *Fú wù yuán, diǎn cài.* – “Waiter, I’d like to order.”  

### 6.2.  Basic Ordering Templates  

| Template | Pinyin | English |
|----------|--------|---------|
| **我要一份…** | wǒ yào yí fèn … | “I want one portion of …” |
| **请给我…** | qǐng gěi wǒ … | “Please give me …” |
| **来一份…** | lái yí fèn … | “Bring a serving of …” |

**Examples**

* **我要一份炸酱面。** – *Wǒ yào yí fèn zhá jiàng miàn.* – “I’d like a bowl of zhajiang noodles.”  
* **请给我一杯绿茶。** – *Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi lǜ chá.* – “Please give me a cup of green tea.”  

### 6.3.  Modifying the Order  

| Modification | Pinyin | English |
|--------------|--------|---------|
| **不要辣** | bù yào là | “Not spicy” |
| **少盐** | shǎo yán | “Less salt” |
| **加鸡蛋** | jiā jī dàn | “Add an egg” |
| **换成米饭** | huàn chéng mǐ fàn | “Replace with rice” |
| **不要花生** | bù yào huā shēng | “No peanuts” |

**Sample Sentence**  
> **请把这道菜** **不要辣** **，** **少盐** **，** **加鸡蛋**。  
> *Qǐng bǎ zhè dào cài bù yào là, shǎo yán, jiā jī dàn.* – “Please make this dish not spicy, less salty, and add an egg.”

### 6.4.  Expressing Satisfaction or Complaints  

| Phrase | Pinyin | English |
|--------|--------|---------|
| **很好吃！** | hěn hǎo chī! | “Very tasty!” |
| **味道很好。** | wèi dào hěn hǎo. | “The flavor is great.” |
| **太咸了。** | tài xián le. | “It’s too salty.” |
| **这道菜有点凉。** | zhè dào cài yǒu diǎn liáng. | “This dish is a bit cold.” |
| **可以帮我换一下吗？** | kě yǐ bāng wǒ huàn yí xià ma? | “Could you help me replace it?” |
| **对不起，我想要退菜。** | duì bu qǐ, wǒ xiǎng yào tuì cài. | “Sorry, I’d like to return the dish.” |

When giving a complaint, start with **对不起** or **请问** to keep the tone courteous.

---

## 7.  Payment Phrases  

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---------|--------|---------|
| **多少钱** | duō shǎo qián | how much (price) |
| **一共** | yī gòng | total (amount) |
| **可以刷卡吗？** | kě yǐ shuā kǎ ma? | “Can I swipe a card?” |
| **请给我收据** | qǐng gěi wǒ shōu jù | “Please give me a receipt.” |
| **找零** | zhǎo líng | change (money returned) |
| **现金** | xiàn jīn | cash |
| **支付宝** | zhī fù bǎo | Alipay (mobile payment) |
| **微信支付** | wēi xìn zhī fù | WeChat Pay |

### 7.1.  Asking the Total  

* **请问，一共多少钱？** – *Qǐng wèn, yī gòng duō shǎo qián?* – “May I ask, what’s the total?”  

### 7.2.  Paying by Card or Mobile  

* **可以刷卡吗？** – *Kě yǐ shuā kǎ ma?* – “Can I pay by card?”  
* **可以用微信支付吗？** – *Kě yǐ yòng wēi xìn zhī fù ma?* – “Can I use WeChat Pay?”  

### 7.3.  Requesting a Receipt  

* **请给我收据。** – *Qǐng gěi wǒ shōu jù.* – “Please give me a receipt.”  

### 7.4.  Handling Change  

* **请找零钱。** – *Qǐng zhǎo líng qián.* – “Please give me change.”  

---

## 8.  Putting It All Together: Two Real‑World Dialogues  

### 8.1.  Dialogue 1 – Buying a Souvenir  

| Speaker | Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|--------|---------|--------|---------|
| **A** (Customer) | 你好，请问这件**T‑恤**多少钱？ | Nǐ hǎo, qǐng wèn zhè jiàn T‑xù duō shǎo qián? | “Hello, may I ask how much this T‑shirt is?” |
| **B** (Shopkeeper) | 这件是八十块。 | Zhè jiàn shì bā shí kuài. | “It’s 80 yuan.” |
| **A** | 有没有颜色更淡的？ | Yǒu méi yǒu yán sè gèng dàn de? | “Do you have a lighter color?” |
| **B** | 有，白色的。 | Yǒu, bái sè de. | “Yes, the white one.” |
| **A** | 能不能便宜一点？七十块可以吗？ | Néng bù néng pián yì diǎn? Qī shí kuài kě yǐ ma? | “Could it be a bit cheaper? 70 yuan okay?” |
| **B** | 好的，七十五块。 | Hǎo de, qī shí wǔ kuài. | “Alright, 75 yuan.” |
| **A** | 请给我收据。 | Qǐng gěi wǒ shōu jù. | “Please give me a receipt.” |
| **B** | 好的，一共七十五块。 | Hǎo de, yī gòng qī shí wǔ kuài. | “Okay, the total is 75 yuan.” |
| **A** | 可以刷卡吗？ | Kě yǐ shuā kǎ ma? | “Can I pay by card?” |
| **B** | 可以。 | Kě yǐ. | “Yes.” |
| **A** | 谢谢！ | Xiè xie! | “Thank you!” |

### 8.2.  Dialogue 2 – Ordering at a Restaurant  

| Speaker | Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|--------|---------|--------|---------|
| **C** (Waiter) | 您好，请问几位？ | Nín hǎo, qǐng wèn jǐ wèi? | “Hello, how many people?” |
| **D** (Diner) | 两位。请给我们**菜单**。 | Liǎng wèi. Qǐng gěi wǒ men cài dān. | “Two. Please give us the menu.” |
| **D** | 我们要**一碗牛肉面**，**不要辣**，**少盐**。 | Wǒ men yào yì wǎn niú ròu miàn, bù yào là, shǎo yán. | “We’d like a bowl of beef noodles, not spicy, less salty.” |
| **C** | 好的。**还有**什么？ | Hǎo de. Hái yǒu shén me? | “Okay. Anything else?” |
| **D** | 再来一份**炒饭**，**加鸡蛋**。 | Zài lái yí fèn chǎo fàn, jiā jī dàn. | “Also a serving of fried rice, add an egg.” |
| **C** | 饮料呢？ | Yǐn liào ne? | “What about drinks?” |
| **D** | 两杯**绿茶**，谢谢。 | Liǎng bēi lǜ chá, xiè xie. | “Two cups of green tea, thank you.” |
| **C** | 好的，请稍等。 | Hǎo de, qǐng shāo děng. | “Alright, please wait a moment.” |
| *(After eating)* | **服务员**，**这道菜太咸了**，**可以帮我换一下**吗？ | Fú wù yuán, zhè dào cài tài xián le, kě yǐ bāng wǒ huàn yí xià ma? | “Waiter, this dish is too salty, could you help me replace it?” |
| **C** | 对不起，我马上为您处理。 | Duì bu qǐ, wǒ mǎ shàng wèi nín chǔ lǐ. | “Sorry, I’ll take care of it right away.” |
| *(When ready to pay)* | **请问，一共多少钱？** | Qǐng wèn, yī gòng duō shǎo qián? | “May I ask, what’s the total?” |
| **C** | 一共一百二十块。 | Yī gòng yī bǎi èr shí kuài. | “The total is 120 yuan.” |
| **D** | 可以用**微信支付**吗？ | Kě yǐ yòng wēi xìn zhī fù ma? | “Can I use WeChat Pay?” |
| **C** | 可以。 | Kě yǐ. | “Yes.” |
| **D** | 谢谢，**请给我收据**。 | Xiè xie, qǐng gěi wǒ shōu jù. | “Thank you, please give me a receipt.” |
| **C** | 好的，祝您用餐愉快！ | Hǎo de, zhù nín yòng cān yú kuài! | “Alright, enjoy your meal!” |

These dialogues illustrate the flow from greeting, through ordering, to payment, and finally expressing gratitude. Practice them aloud, swapping roles, to internalize the patterns.

---

## 9.  Practice Exercises  

### 9.1.  Fill‑in‑the‑Blank (Shopping)  

1. “请问，这件**______**多少钱？” (shirt) → **衬衫** (*chèn shān*)  
2. “**______**可以刷卡吗？” (restaurant) → **餐厅** (*cān tīng*)  
3. “**______**要少盐，**______**不要辣。” (noodles, soup) → **面条** (*miàn tiáo*), **汤** (*tāng*)  

### 9.2.  Match the English to the Chinese  

| English | Chinese |
|---------|---------|
| “Can I have a receipt?” | 请给我收据。 |
| “Is there a discount?” | 有折扣吗？ |
| “I’d like two plates of dumplings.” | 我要两盘饺子。 |
| “This dish is too cold.” | 这道菜有点凉。 |
| “Can I pay with Alipay?” | 可以用支付宝吗？ |

### 9.3.  Role‑Play Prompt  

*Scenario:* You are at a market stall selling **手工艺品** (hand‑made crafts). The vendor offers a **钥匙扣** (keychain) for **20元**. Practice the following sequence:

1. Ask the price and whether there is a **different color**.  
2. Request a **discount** if you buy **three**.  
3. Pay with a **credit card** and ask for a **receipt**.  

Write the dialogue in Chinese, then translate it to English.

---

## 10.  Tips for Real‑World Success  

* **Listen for the measure word** – The vendor may say “这件” (*zhè jiàn*) for clothing, “这个” (*zhè ge*) for a generic item, or “这条” (*zhè tiáo*) for a scarf. Echo the same measure word in your reply; it sounds natural.  
* **Use “请”** early in the sentence to soften a request, especially when you are asking for a modification (“请不要辣”).  
* **Combine two requests with “和”** – “请给我一碗面和一杯水” (*qǐng gěi wǒ yì wǎn miàn hé yì bēi shuǐ*) – “Please give me a bowl of noodles and a glass of water.”  
* **When you don’t understand a price**, repeat the number back: “**八十块**？” (*bā shí kuài?*) – “80 yuan?” This confirms you heard correctly.  
* **Smile and say “谢谢”** after the transaction. A simple thank‑you goes a long way in Chinese culture.

---

## Key Takeaways  

* **Price, size, and availability** are expressed with **多少钱**, **尺寸**, and **有/没有**.  
* **Polite bargaining** uses **能不能** and **请问**; always end with **谢谢** to show appreciation.  
* **Ordering food** follows the pattern **我要 + measure word + dish**, and modifications use **不要**, **少**, **加**, etc.  
* **Payment** relies on **一共多少钱**, **可以刷卡吗**, and **请给我收据**.  
* Mastering **measure words** (reviewed in Module 4) is essential for sounding natural in both shopping and dining contexts.  
* Practice the sample dialogues and exercises; speaking them aloud will reinforce the tone, rhythm, and polite forms needed for everyday Chinese interactions.

modules.title: Module 9: Short Dialogues and Cultural Etiquette
modules.content:
## Warm‑up Scenario: A Day in Shanghai You have just arrived at Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station. The rain has stopped, the city buzzes with traffic, and a friendly local—**xiǎo Lǐ**—offers to help you find your hotel. In the next few minutes you will practice greetings, ask for directions, buy a train ticket, shop for a souvenir, and order dinner—all while noticing the subtle etiquette that makes the interaction smooth. --- ## Dialogue 1 – Polite Greeting & Self‑Introduction | Mandarin (Simplified) | Pinyin | English | |-----------------------|--------|---------| | 你好！
我叫 **Anna**，很高兴认识你。 | Nǐ hǎo!
Wǒ jiào **Anna**, hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ. | Hello!
My name is **Anna**, nice to meet you. | | 你好，Anna！
我叫 **小李**，欢迎来到上海。 | Nǐ hǎo, Anna!
Wǒ jiào **Xiǎo Lǐ**, huānyíng lái dào Shànghǎi. | Hello, Anna!
I’m **Xiao Li**, welcome to Shanghai. | **Key points** - **Nǐ hǎo** (你好) uses the **third tone** on *hǎo*—review the tone pattern from *Module 1*. - The verb **叫** (jiào) “to be called” follows the subject‑verb‑object order introduced in *Module 6*. - **很高兴** (hěn gāoxìng) is a polite way to express “very happy.” The adverb **很** (hěn) softens the statement, a common courtesy in Chinese. **Practice tip**: Mirror the sentence structure, then swap names with a partner. Pay attention to the tone contour of *hǎo* and *gāoxìng*. --- ## Dialogue 2 – Asking for Directions (Travel) | Mandarin (Simplified) | Pinyin | English | |-----------------------|--------|---------| | 请问，**外滩**怎么走？ | Qǐngwèn, **Wàitān** zěnme zǒu? | Excuse me, how do I get to the Bund? | | 往前走，左转，走到**南京东路**，再右转。大约 **十五分钟**。 | Wǎng qián zǒu, zuǒ zhuǎn, zǒu dào **Nánjīng Dōng Lù**, zài yòu zhuǎn. Dàyuē **shíwǔ fēnzhōng**. | Go straight, turn left, walk to **East Nanjing Road**, then turn right. About **15 minutes**. | | 谢谢！
您真好！ | Xièxiè!
Nín zhēn hǎo! | Thank you!
You’re so kind! | **Key points** - **请问** (qǐngwèn) “may I ask” adds politeness; it appears in many request forms. - Directional verbs **走** (zǒu) “to walk/go” and **转** (zhuǎn) “to turn” were introduced in *Module 7*. - **您** (nín) is the respectful second‑person pronoun—use it when speaking to strangers or elders. **Cultural cue**: When giving directions, a slight nod and open palm gesture are common. It signals willingness to help and makes the explanation clearer. --- ## Dialogue 3 – Buying a Train Ticket (Travel) | Mandarin (Simplified) | Pinyin | English | |-----------------------|--------|---------| | 两张 **去北京** 的高铁票，**硬座**。 | Liǎng zhāng **qù Běijīng** de gāotiě piào, **yìngzuò**. | Two high‑speed tickets to Beijing, **hard seat**. | | 好的，**成人**票每张 **¥560**。请您 **先付**。 | Hǎo de, **chéngrén** piào měi zhāng **¥560**. Qǐng nín **xiān fù**. | OK, adult tickets are **¥560** each. Please **pay first**. | | **这里**。
谢谢！
请问 **取票口** 在哪里？ | **Zhè lǐ**.
Xièxiè!
Qǐngwèn **qǔ piào kǒu** zài nǎlǐ? | **Here**.
Thank you!
Where is the **ticket‑collection window**? | | 在左边的 **自动售票机**，您可以自行 **取票**。 | Zài zuǒ biān de **zìdòng shòupiào jī**, nín kěyǐ zìxíng **qǔ piào**. | It’s at the left **self‑service ticket machine**, you can **collect the ticket** yourself. | **Key points** - **硬座** (yìngzuò) “hard seat” contrasts with **软座** (ruǎnzuò) “soft seat.” The noun‑modifier pattern follows *Module 4*’s measure‑word usage. - **先付** (xiān fù) “pay first” uses the verb **付** (fù) from *Module 6*. - Numbers and currency (¥560) rely on the numeral system from *Module 3*. **Etiquette tip**: When handing over money, present both the cash and any receipt **with both hands** (see the next section). This demonstrates respect and attentiveness. --- ## Dialogue 4 – Shopping for Souvenirs (Shopping) | Mandarin (Simplified) | Pinyin | English | |-----------------------|--------|---------| | 这个 **手工布包** 多少钱？ | Zhè ge **shǒugōng bù bāo** duōshǎo qián? | How much is this **hand‑made cloth bag**? | | **八十块**，可以再 **便宜** 五块。 | **Bāshí kuài**, kěyǐ zài **piányí** wǔ kuài. | **80 yuan**, can be **discounted** by five yuan. | | 好的，我要两个。
